title: Descent from local torsion-controlled triples
statement: Let $X$ be Noetherian, $J$ ideal sheaf data, $H$ coherent, $N$ coherent formal, and $\delta:N\to\widehat H$ a map [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in A}$ be an open cover. For each $i$ let $H_i$ be coherent with underlying module $H|_{U_i}$ and let $\gamma_i:(\widehat H)|_{U_i}\simeq\widehat H_i$ respect the quotient projections. Suppose for each $i$ there exist a coherent $F_i$, a map $a_i:F_i\to H_i$, and an isomorphism $\beta_i:N|_{U_i}\simeq\widehat F_i$, satisfying $\delta|_{U_i}\circ\gamma_i=\beta_i\circ\widehat a_i$, and some positive power of $J|_{U_i}$ annihilates the kernel and cokernel of $a_i$. Then there exist global $F,a,\beta$ satisfying the same factorization, with a single positive power of $J$ annihilating the kernel and cokernel of $a$. No component-annihilation hypothesis on $\delta$ is assumed; the local triples are supplied.

proof.text: Restrict supplied triples to overlaps, comparing completions by their quotient projections. Lift the formal comparison and its inverse using torsion-controlled completion homomorphism lifting. Completion extensionality identifies both composites with identities, and proves uniqueness. On triple overlaps uniqueness implies the cocycle identity. Intersections need not be affine.

proof.text: Glue the sheaves and maps by sheaf-of-modules descent; coherence descends locally. Glue the formal component comparison maps and their inverses levelwise. Their transition equations and factorization equations hold locally and hence globally, producing the global beta and its factorization.

Choose a finite subcover. Take the maximum of its positive bounds and 1, using bound 1 for an empty cover. Higher powers factor through lower powers. Exact restriction identifies the restricted global kernels and cokernels with the local ones, so the common power kills both locally. An ideal product vanishing on a cover is zero, giving global annihilation.

theorem torsionControlled_algebraization_descent
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (H : CoherentModules X) (N : CoherentFormalModule X J)
    (δ : N ⟶ (completion X J).obj H)
    (ι : Type u) (U : ι → X.Opens) (hcover : (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤)
    (Hlocal : ∀ i, CoherentModules (U i).toScheme)
    (hHlocal : ∀ i, (Hlocal i).obj = (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι).obj H.obj)
    (γ : ∀ i, ((completion X J).obj H).obj ⋙
      Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι ≅
        formalCompletionSystem (J.comap (U i).ι) (Hlocal i).obj)
    (hγ : ∀ (i : ι) (n : ℕ),
      (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι).map
          (formalModuleQuotientπ J (n + 1) H.obj) ≫ (γ i).hom.app (op n) =
        eqToHom (hHlocal i).symm ≫
          formalModuleQuotientπ (J.comap (U i).ι) (n + 1) (Hlocal i).obj)
    (hlocal : ∀ i, ∃ (F : CoherentModules (U i).toScheme) (a : F ⟶ Hlocal i)
      (β : N.obj ⋙ Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι ≅
        formalCompletionSystem (J.comap (U i).ι) F.obj),
      Functor.whiskerRight δ.hom (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U i).ι) ≫ (γ i).hom =
        β.hom ≫ formalCompletionMap (J.comap (U i).ι) a.hom ∧
      (∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧
        IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
          (Scheme.idealSheafPower (J.comap (U i).ι).toModulesι s).2 (kernel a.hom)) ∧
        IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
          (Scheme.idealSheafPower (J.comap (U i).ι).toModulesι s).2 (cokernel a.hom)))) :
    ∃ (F : CoherentModules X) (a : F ⟶ H) (β : N ≅ (completion X J).obj F),
      δ = β.hom ≫ (completion X J).map a ∧
      (∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧
        IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
          (kernel a.hom)) ∧
        IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2
          (cokernel a.hom)))
